# 什么是查询扇出（Query Fan-Out）？

- 原标题：What Is Query Fan-Out?
- 作者：Flavio Amiel Roborank 创始人
- 原文更新日期：2026-07-14
- 原文：https://roborank.io/glossary/query-fan-out/
- 栏目：[AI Search & GEO](https://roborank.io/ai-search/)
- 说明：中文全文翻译，后附英文原文。原文中的数据、观点、平台说明及推广内容均按原文保留，未经独立验证。

---

## 中文全文

查询扇出，是 Google 为 AI Mode 和 AI Overviews 所用的一种技术命名：系统将用户的一个查询拆解为多个相关子查询，在搜索索引及其他数据源中并行执行，再把综合结果合成为一个答案。因此，某个页面可能因为一个从未明确针对过的子查询而获得引用。

### 核心要点

- Google 在 2025 年 3 月介绍 AI Mode 的文章中公开命名了这项技术：系统会“围绕子主题、跨多个数据源，同时发起多个相关搜索”。
- 用户的一个问题会扩展成多次后台搜索，因此与你竞争的页面，是针对每个子查询选择的，而不是针对最初那个关键词。
- 页面可能因为一个从未专门为之撰写的子查询而被引用，这既扩大了你能赢得的范围，也扩大了竞争对手可能夺走的范围。
- 由于检索针对多个并行子查询展开，获胜内容会清楚回答一个具体子问题，而不是肤浅覆盖一个宽泛主关键词。

### 查询扇出如何运作

传统搜索接收你输入的字符串，将它与索引匹配，再返回按排名排列的链接列表。查询扇出在这一过程前面增加了规划步骤。系统还没检索任何内容时，就会先阅读你的问题，判断其中实际包含哪些更小的问题，同时发起一组相关搜索，再将所有结果收回来，写成一个答案。

Google 对该机制的描述很直白。在 2025 年 3 月介绍 AI Mode 的文章中，公司表示，这项功能“使用一种‘查询扇出’技术，围绕子主题、跨多个数据源，同时发起多个相关搜索，再将这些结果汇总，提供易于理解的回答”。这句话包含了整个过程：拆解、并行搜索、合并。

拆解这一步打破了旧有假设。假设你问“老房子装热泵值不值得”，引擎不会只是搜索这一串文字，而是把它展开成它推断你关心的子问题：老建筑的安装成本、保温较差时的效率损失、现有散热器是否适用、地区补贴等，并分别搜索。这些子查询既会从支撑传统蓝色链接结果的同一索引中提取候选内容，也会使用知识图谱和购物数据等其他来源。因此，答案实际上经过了[事实依据锚定](https://roborank.io/glossary/grounding/)：模型不是凭记忆回答，而是根据这些子查询刚刚检索到的文档回答。

由于检索针对每个子查询分别进行，每次竞争的范围也会重新划定。系统并不是只围绕主关键词整体评判你的页面，而是分别针对扇出产生的每个子查询评判它——而你永远看不到那份列表。一个页面可能被某个子问题选中，却被另外四个忽略。这与[检索增强生成](https://roborank.io/glossary/retrieval-augmented-generation/)背后的“先检索、再合成”模式相同，只是应用到了搜索规模，并由 Google 为自己的产品起了这个名称。

接下来，合成步骤会把获胜文档中的段落拼成一个回答，通常附带引用。这项技术可以随着任务规模扩大：Google 表示，Deep Search“使用相同的查询扇出技术，但将其提升到新的层次”，通过数百次搜索汇总出一份引用完备的报告。想法相同，只是扇出的范围更大。

### 查询扇出示例

最清晰的真实例子，就是 Google 自己发布的例子。产品副总裁 Robby Stein 在 [2025 年 3 月的文章](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/ai-mode-search/)中宣布推出 [AI Mode](https://roborank.io/glossary/google-ai-mode/)时，不只是说这项功能很聪明，还明确指出了背后的机制。文章写道，AI Mode“使用一种‘查询扇出’技术，围绕子主题、跨多个数据源，同时发起多个相关搜索，再将这些结果汇总，提供易于理解的回答”。同一篇文章也解释，这正是 AI Mode 相比单次传统搜索“可以更深入探索网络”的原因：它运行的不是一个查询，而是多个查询。

以一个具体问题来看。假设用户要求 AI Mode 比较两款适合通勤的中端公路自行车。传统搜索会针对这个短语返回排名列表，围绕“最佳通勤公路自行车”优化得最好的评测网站，往往赢得点击。在查询扇出机制下，引擎会同时发起一组子搜索：长距离舒适度、适应湿滑道路的轮胎间隙、重量、零部件可靠性，以及当前零售价格，并为每一项检索候选内容。一篇从未提到这两款车型的车架几何讲解，可能被提取来回答舒适度子查询；一个论坛帖子可能回答可靠性；零售页面则回答价格。Google 自己的表述也确认了“多个数据源”这一点：扇出不只搜索网页，还会涉及购物和结构化数据。最终答案由这些材料共同组成，每个贡献页面都因自己回答得最好的那一小部分而获得引用。

意想不到的收益和风险就在同一个过程中出现。那篇舒适度讲解，因为一个它从未打算参与的产品比较而获得引用，这种额外收益是你可以主动设计争取的。但主关键词排名第一的自行车评测，也可能完全被跳过，只因它把具体子问题的答案埋在宽泛综述下面。排名没有带来任何帮助，因为引擎寻找的是子问题的答案，而不是那个它曾经占据优势的关键词。Google 的 Deep Search 扩展进一步放大了影响：同一篇文章提到，它可以“发起数百次搜索”来构建附引用的报告，这意味着数百场独立的子查询竞争，每一次都可能带来引用，也可能让你被遗漏。

### 人们常犯的错误

人们本能地会针对用户输入的问题优化。但查询扇出意味着，引擎实际上并不是在搜索那个问题，而是在搜索它判断这个问题包含的八到十个更小的问题，你又看不到那份列表。我见过一个页面被纳入某项比较的答案，虽然它从未明确提及那项比较，仅仅因为其中一段恰好清楚解决了引擎临时生成的子问题。实际应对方式，是不再只为一个关键词写一页内容，而是在页面中安排围绕主题的每个合理子问题的独立答案。你不再只是为一个查询争排名，而是在备好一个货架，引擎会来取用，却不告诉你它原本想找什么。

### 为什么它会重塑内容策略

查询扇出悄悄改变了目标。过去十年，SEO 的基本单位是关键词：选一个词、匹配意图、让页面获得排名。扇出把这个单一目标打散成一组由引擎在内部生成的子查询，并分别针对它们检索。你优化的是一组自己无法看到的问题。

这会改变好页面的样子。围绕一个主关键词深入展开、写成连续长篇叙述，恰恰是扇出机制难以奖励的形态，因为没有哪一段能清楚地回答一个具体子查询。进入答案的页面往往是模块化的：由一组自成一体的部分组成，每部分解决一个具体子问题，而且即使脱离原上下文也仍然成立。因此，[可提取性](https://roborank.io/glossary/extractability/)——段落能否独立被引用——是最能直接将扇出机会转化为引用的属性。

它同时扩大了机会和威胁。页面可能因从未针对的子查询被引用，因此一份结构良好的资源，可以在整个主题集群中累积引用，而不是只覆盖一个词；这正是[生成式引擎优化](https://roborank.io/glossary/generative-engine-optimization/)和[答案引擎优化](https://roborank.io/glossary/answer-engine-optimization/)的核心价值。反过来，你以为属于自己的子查询，也可能由竞争对手的页面提供答案。你们都控制不了扇出过程，只能控制自己的段落能否清楚回答其中的问题。

衡量方式也要跟随机制。当引擎在一个答案背后运行十次子搜索时，平均排名能告诉你的东西很少；因此，扇出可见性要通过[引用份额](https://roborank.io/glossary/citation-share/)这类引用层面的信号追踪：在答案对全部子查询所分配的引用中，你占多少。由此得到的操作建议说起来简单、做起来困难：不要再只为了某个查询的排名而写作，要在页面中准备清楚、可引用的答案，覆盖引擎可能从该查询衍生出的每个合理子问题。

### 常见问题

#### 什么是查询扇出？

它是一种检索技术：搜索系统把用户的一个问题拆成多个相关子查询，在索引及其他数据源中并行执行，再将结果合并成一个 AI 生成的答案。Google 在介绍 AI Mode 和 AI Overviews 时为这一机制命名。

#### “查询扇出”这个术语是谁提出的？

Google。产品副总裁 Robby Stein 在 2025 年 3 月宣布 AI Mode 的博客文章中描述了“查询扇出”技术，后来 Google 又把这一术语用于 AI Overviews 和 Deep Search。这是 Google 自己为该机制起的名称，不是第三方创造的说法。

#### 查询扇出为什么对 SEO 重要？

因为引擎会针对你未曾选定的子查询检索，页面可能因从未明确针对的问题而被引用，也可能在自己的主关键词下被跳过。如今，可见性取决于能否清楚回答多个具体子问题，而不只是为一个宽泛词获得排名。

#### 查询扇出与普通搜索有什么区别？

普通搜索把一个查询与索引匹配，并返回排名列表。查询扇出同时发起多个子查询，从每个子查询中提取候选内容，再合成一个答案。用户看到的是一次回答，但引擎在底层运行的是一组并行搜索。

### 要点总结

查询扇出将竞争单位，从用户输入的关键词，改成引擎由此衍生的一组隐藏子查询。你看不到这份列表，因此持久的策略是充分覆盖、表达清楚：在页面中安排围绕主题的每个合理子问题的独立答案，每个都能单独引用。赢家是那些已经做好准备、能够进入某个答案的页面，即使它们看起来原本并不是在讨论那个问题。

## 英文原文

Query fan-out is a technique, named by Google for AI Mode and AI Overviews, where the system decomposes a single user query into multiple related sub-queries, runs them in parallel against the search index and other data sources, and synthesizes one answer from the combined results — so a page can be cited for a sub-query it never obviously targeted.

### Key Takeaways

- Google publicly named the technique in its March 2025 post introducing AI Mode: the system issues ‘multiple related searches concurrently across subtopics and multiple data sources.’
- One user question expands into many background searches, so the page you compete against is chosen per sub-query, not per original keyword.
- A page can be cited for a sub-query it was never written to target, which widens the surface you can win and the surface a competitor can steal.
- Because retrieval happens across parallel sub-queries, the winning content answers a specific sub-question cleanly rather than covering the broad head term shallowly.

### How Query Fan-Out Works

A traditional search takes the string you typed, matches it against the index, and returns a ranked list of links. Query fan-out inserts a planning step in front of that. Before it retrieves anything, the system reads your question, decides what smaller questions it actually contains, and issues a fan of related searches at once — then it gathers everything back and writes a single answer.

Google describes the mechanism plainly. In its March 2025 post introducing AI Mode, the company said the feature “uses a ‘query fan-out’ technique, issuing multiple related searches concurrently across subtopics and multiple data sources and then brings those results together to provide an easy-to-understand response.” That one sentence contains the whole shape of it: decompose, search in parallel, merge.

The decomposition is the part that breaks old assumptions. Ask “is a heat pump worth it for an old house,” and the engine does not run that string. It expands it into sub-questions it infers you care about — installation cost in older buildings, efficiency loss with poor insulation, whether existing radiators work, regional rebates — and searches each one. Those sub-queries pull candidates from the same index that powers blue-link results, plus other sources like the knowledge graph and shopping data. This is why the answer is a form of [grounding](https://roborank.io/glossary/grounding/): the model is not answering from memory, it is answering from documents its sub-queries just retrieved.

Because retrieval runs per sub-query, the competitive field is redrawn for each one. Your page is not judged against the head term as a whole. It is judged, separately, against every sub-query the fan produced — and you never see that list. A page can be selected for one sub-question and ignored for four others. That is the same retrieve-then-synthesize pattern behind [retrieval-augmented generation](https://roborank.io/glossary/retrieval-augmented-generation/), applied at search scale and named by Google for its own products.

The synthesis step then stitches passages from the winning documents into one response, usually with citations. The technique scales with ambition: Google notes that Deep Search “uses the same query fan-out technique but taken to the next level,” issuing hundreds of searches to assemble a fully-cited report. Same idea, more fan.

### Example of Query Fan-Out

The clearest real example is the one Google published itself. When it announced [AI Mode](https://roborank.io/glossary/google-ai-mode/) in the [March 2025 post](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/ai-mode-search/) by VP of Product Robby Stein, it did not just claim the feature was smart — it named the machinery. AI Mode, the post says, “uses a ‘query fan-out’ technique, issuing multiple related searches concurrently across subtopics and multiple data sources and then brings those results together to provide an easy-to-understand response.” The same post positions this as the reason AI Mode “can dive deeper into the web” than a single traditional search: it is not running one query, it is running many.

Walk it through with a concrete question. Suppose a user asks AI Mode to compare two mid-range road bikes for commuting. A traditional search returns a ranked list for that phrase, and the review site that best optimized for “best commuter road bike” tends to win the click. Under query fan-out, the engine instead fires a set of parallel sub-searches — comfort over long distances, tire clearance for wet roads, weight, component reliability, price at current retailers — and retrieves candidates for each. A frame-geometry explainer that never mentions either bike by name can be pulled in to answer the comfort sub-query. A forum thread can answer reliability. A retailer page answers price. Google’s own framing confirms the “multiple data sources” part: the fan does not just hit web pages, it reaches shopping and structured data too. The final answer is assembled from all of them, and each contributing page earns a citation for the narrow slice it answered best.

That is the counterintuitive payoff and the risk in one motion. The comfort explainer got cited for a comparison it was never written to enter, which is upside you can engineer. But the bike review that ranked #1 for the head term can be skipped entirely if it buried the specific sub-answers under a broad overview — its ranking bought it nothing, because the engine was shopping for sub-questions, not for the keyword it once dominated. Google’s Deep Search extension makes the stakes larger still: the same post notes it can “issue hundreds of searches” to build a cited report, which means hundreds of separate sub-query contests, each a chance to be cited or omitted.

### The thing people get wrong

The instinct is to optimize for the question the user typed. Query fan-out means the engine is not really searching for that question — it is searching for the eight or ten smaller questions it decided the real question contains, and you never see that list. I have watched a page get pulled into an answer for a comparison it never mentioned by name, simply because one of its paragraphs cleanly resolved a sub-question the engine invented on the fly. The practical move is to stop writing one page aimed at one keyword and start seeding a page with self-contained answers to every reasonable sub-question around it. You are not ranking for a query anymore. You are stocking a shelf the engine raids without telling you what it came for.

### Why It Reshapes Content Strategy

Query fan-out quietly moves the target. For a decade the unit of SEO was the keyword — pick one, match intent, rank the page. Fan-out shatters that single target into a spray of sub-queries the engine derives privately, and it retrieves against each of them independently. You are optimizing for a question set you cannot read.

That changes what a good page looks like. Depth on a single head term, expressed as one long flowing narrative, is exactly the shape fan-out struggles to reward, because no single passage answers any one sub-query cleanly. The pages that get pulled into answers tend to be modular: a series of self-contained sections, each resolving one specific sub-question in a block that survives being lifted out of context. This is why [extractability](https://roborank.io/glossary/extractability/) — whether a passage can be quoted in isolation — is the property that most directly translates fan-out into citations.

It also widens both the opportunity and the threat. Because a page can be cited for sub-queries it never targeted, a well-structured resource can accumulate citations across a whole topic cluster rather than a single term — the core promise of [generative engine optimization](https://roborank.io/glossary/generative-engine-optimization/) and [answer engine optimization](https://roborank.io/glossary/answer-engine-optimization/). The flip side is that a competitor’s page can be raided for a sub-query you assumed you owned. Neither of you controls the fan; you only control how cleanly your passages answer the questions inside it.

The measurement follows the mechanism. Average position tells you little when the engine is running ten sub-searches behind one answer, so fan-out visibility is tracked with citation-level signals like [citation share](https://roborank.io/glossary/citation-share/) — your slice of the citations an answer awards across all the sub-queries it ran. The practical instruction that falls out of all this is simple to state and hard to do: stop writing to rank for a query, and start stocking a page with clean, quotable answers to every reasonable sub-question the engine might invent from it.

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### What is query fan-out?

Query fan-out is a retrieval technique where a search system breaks one user question into several related sub-queries, runs them in parallel across its index and other data sources, and merges the results into a single AI-generated answer. Google named it when introducing AI Mode and AI Overviews.

#### Who coined the term query fan-out?

Google. It described the ‘query fan-out’ technique in a March 2025 blog post by VP of Product Robby Stein announcing AI Mode, and reused the term for AI Overviews and Deep Search. It is Google’s own name for the mechanism, not a third-party coinage.

#### Why does query fan-out matter for SEO?

Because the engine retrieves against sub-queries you never chose, a page can be cited for questions it never explicitly targeted — and can be skipped for its main keyword. Visibility now depends on answering many specific sub-questions cleanly, not on ranking one broad term.

#### How is query fan-out different from a normal search?

A normal search matches one query against the index and returns a ranked list. Query fan-out issues many sub-queries at once, pulls candidates from each, then synthesizes one answer. The user sees a single response, but underneath the engine ran a fan of parallel searches.

### The Bottom Line

Query fan-out changes the unit of competition from the keyword a user typed to the fan of hidden sub-queries an engine derives from it. You cannot see that list, so the durable strategy is coverage and cleanliness: seed a page with self-contained answers to every reasonable sub-question around the topic, each quotable on its own. The pages that win are the ones ready to be pulled into an answer for a question they were never obviously about.
